claim_boundary: Source-only deterministic state simulation for content-addressed checkpoints, crash reopening, pivot children, replay, and partial-write recovery. It proves no process restart, provider/model/evaluator execution, Trace append, service activation, promotion, deployment, or fleet recovery.

capabilities.name: build_checkpoint
capabilities.description: Seal a committed action head and state while carrying only hashes for the excluded uncommitted tail.

capabilities.name: recover_latest_checkpoint
capabilities.description: Reopen the latest valid committed generation and discard at most one syntactically partial final record.

capabilities.name: pivot_from_checkpoint
capabilities.description: Derive a child generation from an exact parent checkpoint without mutating the parent.

required: complete ordered content-addressed ancestor-core chain for every nonzero generation
preconditions: generation zero binds the scenario-specific genesis sentinel
each child binds the exact prior checkpoint and prior committed state
every ancestor core is independently hash-recomputed against its exact prefix
actions carry contiguous indices, unique identities, exact predecessor hashes, and recomputed action hashes
a pivot has at least one committed action; an omitted tail is represented only by null/None, never by a falsey alias
a partial record may occur only after the last fully committed checkpoint

output_contract.success: A canonical checkpoint or recovery receipt with exact committed-state identity, excluded tail, generation chain, zero execution counts, and all authority false.
output_contract.failure: A typed blocker; a parseable forged record is never downgraded to a harmless partial write.
output_contract.verification: Rebuild or reopen exact bytes and compare checkpoint, state, predecessor, and recovery receipt hashes.

delta_c.rule: Only the committed action head affects recovered state; uncommitted payloads never enter checkpoint state.
A pivot child binds the exact parent checkpoint and must not mutate it.

out_of_scope: training, promotion, deployment, or fleet rollout

steps: 1. Validate the scenario, generation, predecessor, state, and authority envelope.
2. Recompute every committed and uncommitted action chain hash.
3. Apply only committed actions and seal the checkpoint state.
4. Resolve and validate the full ancestry prefix; reject missing, reordered, duplicated, forked, stale, or cyclic links.
5. On recovery, reject fully parseable invalid records and discard only a final syntactically partial record.
6. For a pivot, build generation n+1 from the exact parent hash and state and recheck the unchanged parent.
7. Repeat reopen/replay and require byte-identical receipts.
done_definition: recovered state equals the latest valid committed state
uncommitted effects are absent from state and checkpoint payload
all execution counters remain zero and all authority remains false
repair_on_failure: repair the first divergent generation, action, state, or predecessor hash and regenerate an immutable successor
never reinterpret a validly parsed forged checkpoint as a partial write

exec_block_rules.when: any runtime, provider, evaluator, Trace, training, promotion, or deployment authority is true
a checkpoint, state, generation, predecessor, action, pivot, or recovery receipt is not exactly derivable
